searchSummary: Maximum-cardinality independent set is separate from inclusion-maximal MIS. Every theorem retains its graph class, adversary and resource model; unreviewed cells are not claims that no algorithms exist.

slices.label: Maximum independent set: space for approximation
slices.task: One pass · deterministic · insertions and deletions · explicit independent set
assumptions: Both bounds have leading exponent s=2−t. Green and red are separated by a few screen pixels only for visibility; that offset does not encode a numerical gap. Logarithmic factors and exact finite-n ranges are retained below. Open endpoints mean fixed t<1 (algorithm) and fixed t<1/2 (lower bound), not inclusion of β=n or β=√n.

results.sourceLocation: Theorem A.1 (folklore algorithm presented in Appendix A)
results.notes: General simple unweighted graphs; vertex set known in advance; Explicit independent vertex set I; Deterministic; 1 ≤ β ≤ n/log₂ n; Partition the vertices into balanced groups, store each induced adjacency matrix, and return the largest exact independent set among the groups. Computation may be exponential. This is a folklore algorithm, not a new algorithm claim.

General simple unweighted graphs; vertex set known in advance; Explicit independent vertex set I; Deterministic; 1 ≤ β ≤ √n/(36 log₂ n); The complement construction uses deletions. Version 2 narrows the earlier version's approximation range following corrections. The preprint statement and model were checked; its proof was not independently certified.

slices.label: Maximum independent set in LOCAL
slices.task: Rounds and approximation; graph classes and probability guarantees stay explicit.
assumptions: Symbolic round bounds, not numerical distances. The upper panel fixes a near-optimal ratio on chordal graphs, with a lower bound even on paths. The lower panel permits a degree-dependent approximation on general graphs.

results.notes: Unweighted chordal graphs; An independent vertex set; each vertex learns its membership; Deterministic; ; Standard LOCAL with unique IDs and initial neighbor knowledge. The algorithm computes the needed decomposition; no tree decomposition is supplied as input.

Even unweighted paths, hence a subclass of chordal graphs; sufficiently large n; An independent vertex set; each vertex learns its membership; Randomized algorithms; expectation guarantee; ; The source states an expected approximation-factor requirement, not a high-probability guarantee. Compare the common 0<ε<1/2 range; no general-graph lower bound for a degree-sized approximation follows.

General unweighted graphs of maximum degree Δ; isolated vertices can be included; An independent vertex set; each vertex learns its membership; With high probability; ; The theorem is stated for maximum-weight independent set; assigning every vertex unit weight gives this cardinality result. It works in CONGEST and therefore also LOCAL. Unique IDs and a polynomial upper bound on n are assumed. This is a weaker quality target than a (1+ε)-approximation; its theorem does not require maximality.
